brief.analysis: Defense stocks are being carried by a durable global re-arming cycle — 2025 world military spending hit roughly $2.63 trillion and budgets keep rising — so the sector's lead over the market is fundamentally earned, not a dislocation. Crucially, measured against its own upward trend the ratio is already slightly below fair value, meaning there is no genuine stretch to short in the first place, the confirming trend hasn't even turned down, and the historical hit rate here is weak. The old five-year average is a target the world has structurally moved away from.
brief.report_line: Avoid shorting defense-versus-market: rising global military budgets have permanently lifted the sector, the relationship shows no real overshoot once you account for its rising trend, and the downtrend isn't even confirmed.

brief.analysis: Central banks have permanently lifted how much of the world's savings sit in gold, so gold's 44% run in 2025 wasn't just a spike — the old five-year average of this ratio (which implies gold falling another ~19% versus stocks) is a stale target that assumes a world that no longer exists. Measured against gold's own rising trend rather than a flat line, this ratio is already sitting right at fair value (the trend-adjusted reading is essentially zero even though the flat-mean reading still looks stretched), and the sensible 200-day target has already been hit. The near-term snap-back gold's recent pullback offers is real and the trade has a perfect track record, but do not chase it toward the old mean.
brief.report_line: Short gold-versus-stocks is fine for a quick give-back and its first target is already met, but size it small: central-bank buying has raised gold's floor and the old average is no longer a place gold has to return to.

brief.analysis: Chipmakers' huge lead over the broad tech index is built on a genuine multi-year wave of AI infrastructure spending with real earnings behind it, so the five-year average — which implies chips give back a punishing 64% versus tech — is not a target the world will honor. Even measured against its own upward trend the ratio is still meaningfully stretched, so a pullback to the more realistic 200-day level (~11% of give-back) is a live, well-tested trade. The risk is that you're shorting the single strongest structural story in the market.
brief.report_line: Short semiconductors-versus-tech only to the nearer moving-average target for about an 11% give-back; the deeper old-average target ignores that the AI capex boom has structurally re-rated chips, so keep size modest.

brief.analysis: Miners nearly doubled riding the same gold-and-copper rally that is now correcting, so a give-back is genuinely underway and the trade rides that tailwind — but this is a cyclical commodity swing, not a permanent shift, so the relationship should revert. The offsets are that the deeper old-average target (~25% of give-back) is far away, the trend-adjusted stretch is only moderate, and the winning track record rests on just two prior episodes. The nearer moving-average target is already met, so the easy money may be behind it.
brief.report_line: Short metals-and-mining-versus-market is workable as the gold-driven commodity spike unwinds, but the evidence base is thin and the first target is already hit — take it small and don't reach for the old average.

brief.analysis: Silver went parabolic to around $100 and ran far ahead of gold, and the correction now underway is textbook give-back rather than a broken relationship — analysts frame the ~30% silver pullback as normal mean reversion, not a trend reversal. Measured against its own trend the stretch is only moderate, the first target is already met, and the deeper move toward the old average is credible because silver is simply handing back a spike. This is the cleanest reversion in the book, though silver has genuinely re-rated somewhat, so the very last leg down may not fully complete.
brief.report_line: Short silver-versus-gold is the highest-quality reversion here — silver overshot in a parabola and is already unwinding — but recognize silver's floor has risen, so don't count on it retracing all the way to its old average.
